page_placements.theme: Architectural changes shift loss levels and efficiency frontiers

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure and table content is flattened in the extracted text, so individual architecture-sweep cells cannot be assigned confidently.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports validation-loss scaling curves across compute budgets and an architecture sweep, testing aspects of the scaling claim in a different model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports downstream benchmark scores for Baseline and AttnRes; these compare residual methods, not downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss. They are recorded as findings with versions ["none"]. The paper's cited scaling-law results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: An architecture paper (AttnRes) that uses scaling laws mainly as a tool to compare residual designs. Two of its own results still bear on the claim in a new setting: MoE models with hybrid KDA/MLA attention. First, a five-size PreNorm baseline whose validation loss is fit as a power law in compute over roughly 0.5–5 PFLOP/s-days (V1). Second, a fixed-compute, fixed-active-parameter 5×5 depth/width/head sweep for the baseline (V4). Neither repeats Kaplan or Hoffmann's method exactly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that AttnRes beats the PreNorm baseline across the compute range with a similar slope, and that Block AttnRes (~8 blocks) recovers most of Full AttnRes's gain and equals 1.25× baseline compute. At 48B/3B-active on 1.4T tokens, AttnRes mitigates PreNorm dilution and matches or beats the baseline on all benchmarks. In the fixed-budget sweep, AttnRes shifts the optimum toward deeper, narrower models.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a changed residual architecture (AttnRes) against a PreNorm baseline, fitting validation loss against compute across five model sizes. It does not reproduce the original parameter/token sweeps or test compute-optimal parameter-token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported architecture optimum differs between baseline and AttnRes in the fixed-budget sweep; the study also reports loss changes across block sizes, but those block-size ablations are not tests of the claim versions recorded here.

fits_no_version.finding: AttnRes matches or beats the PreNorm baseline on 15 downstream benchmarks after the same 48B/1.4T-token recipe. MMLU-Pro is tied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Not a scaling-law claim. It is a residual-architecture comparison at a single scale.

fits_no_version.finding: At equal compute, Block AttnRes matches a baseline trained with about 1.25× more compute. All variants share a similar power-law slope (−0.057 to −0.058).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural changes to residual connections shift the scaling-law coefficient but not the exponent. This fits no listed version.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the scaling fits or benchmark comparisons. The compute sweep changes model size and token count together, so it does not isolate their effects. The architecture-sweep heatmap is flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable extraction of all individual configuration values.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant results were omitted. Individual values for the 25 architecture-sweep cells in Fig. 7 were not separately extracted because the supplied flattened figure text does not support reliable assignment; the paper's explicit aggregate comparison and optima are recorded in R4.

untested.parts: Several orders of magnitude (only about one decade of compute); separate scaling in parameters or tokens with the other not a bottleneck.
Whole version: no extrapolation from small fits to much larger runs is checked. The 48B/1.4T model is not compared to the fitted curve.
Whole version: no parameter-vs-token compute-optimal allocation.
Other parameter counts and compute budgets (one budget, ≈2.3e8 active params); architecture details beyond depth, width and head count.
Whole version: downstream scores are compared only between residual methods at one scale.
Whole version: no comparison of fitting choices or setups for the exponents.

missing.what: Baseline loss spread across the 25 shape configurations at fixed compute and params. It ranges from 1.847 (optimum, dmodel/Lb≈60, H/Lb 0.3) to 2.017 (dmodel/Lb 15, H/Lb 0.7), and is about 1.847–1.909 for dmodel/Lb ≥30. AttnRes spread is 1.802–1.954.
Per-size validation losses behind the compute fits: baseline 1.931/1.895/1.829/1.766/1.719 across 194M–528M activated params.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling-law material is used as an evaluation tool for a new residual design, so the bearing on the claim is incidental and narrow. V1 evidence spans about one decade of compute, with parameters and tokens co-varied and no fit diagnostics. The V4 evidence (Fig. 7 heatmap) is the most claim-relevant result, but the record captured only the method gap. No uncertainty is reported anywhere. This is a preprint/technical report, and the study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests validation loss against compute in the reported sweep, but does not independently vary parameters, tokens, and compute to establish their separate scaling relationships or that the other two are not bottlenecks.
No reported test of power-law fits from small runs predicting substantially larger runs.
The fixed-compute architecture sweep reallocates architecture, not the parameter-versus-token split; it does not test how compute-optimal parameter and token counts grow with compute.
Tests a fixed-compute and fixed-active-parameter depth/width/head sweep, not a broad range of all architecture details or parameter counts.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested.
Downstream scores are compared between residual methods, but the study does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The study reports fit curves for its variants but does not test how fitting choices or setup changes alter exponents or compute-optimal allocations, or whether curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: PreNorm baseline
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss against training compute across five model sizes.
rows.measure: Validation loss as a function of compute; fitted power law
rows.note: The paper states that the baseline follows this fit. The fit is over the reported compute sweep, not an independent test of parameter, token, and compute scaling.
rows.check: The link is fine, but the compute range is only about one decade (0.5–5 PFLOP/s-days). Params and tokens grow together (194M–528M; 38.7B–119B), and no goodness of fit is reported. The per-size losses in Table 2 (1.931→1.719) fall monotonically.

rows.subject: Block AttnRes
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss against training compute across five model sizes, using approximately 8 blocks.
rows.measure: Validation loss as a function of compute; fitted power law
rows.note: The authors state that the variant consistently has lower loss across the compute range.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (Block AttnRes) set against the baseline. It bears on V1 only in that its loss also follows a power law in compute. The comparison with the baseline is not a claim result.

rows.subject: Full AttnRes
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss against training compute across five model sizes.
rows.measure: Validation loss as a function of compute; fitted power law
rows.note: The authors state that the variant consistently has lower loss across the compute range.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (Full AttnRes) compared with the baseline, as for R2. Only its power-law form bears on V1.

rows.subject: AttnRes architecture sweep (Block AttnRes in the comparison)
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained; training compute fixed at approximately 6.5 × 10^19 FLOPs
rows.operation_detail: Sweep 25 depth/width/head configurations under fixed compute and active-parameter budgets; compare validation loss with the corresponding baseline configuration.
rows.baseline: Corresponding baseline architecture sweep; baseline optimum 1.847 at dmodel/Lb ≈ 60
rows.value: AttnRes has lower loss in all 25 configurations, by 0.019–0.063; its optimum is 1.802 at dmodel/Lb ≈ 45
rows.note: The authors report the sweep-wide comparison and optima explicitly. The extracted heatmap does not reliably support assigning every individual cell to its configuration.
rows.check: As recorded, the row measures the AttnRes-minus-baseline gap across configurations. That is a method comparison, not how much shape changes loss at fixed parameters. The V4-relevant measure is the spread of baseline (and AttnRes) loss across the 25 cells, which the row omits; see missing. The flattened heatmap appears to swap one cell (1.954/1.858) in the H/Lb=0.7 row.

source_check.correct: Subject: AttnRes architecture sweep; §5.4.1 and Fig. 7 do not specify Full versus Block AttnRes. AttnRes improves all 25 configurations by 0.019–0.063; baseline optimum: loss 1.847 at dmodel/Lb≈60; AttnRes optimum: loss 1.802 at dmodel/Lb≈45; both optima at H/Lb≈0.3.
source_check.problem: The identification as Block AttnRes is unsupported; the recorded method-comparison gap alone cannot determine V4.

relationships.condition: PreNorm MoE baseline, five sizes, ~0.5–5 PFLOP/s-days, cosine schedule
relationships.reason: R1: loss falls with compute and is fit by L = 1.891·C^-0.057. AttnRes variants show the same form (R2, R3). Only about one decade is covered, with no fit statistics.
relationships.display_finding: Baseline loss fitted L = 1.891·C^−0.057, and AttnRes variants followed the same functional form over about one decade of compute.

source_check.reason: R1 reports L=1.891×C^-0.057; R2 and R3 report similar power-law fits. Support is confined to the tested compute range; several-orders scaling and independent parameter/token effects are untested.

relationships.condition: Baseline, fixed compute ≈6.5e19 FLOPs and ≈2.3e8 active params, dmodel/Lb 30–75, H/Lb 0.3–0.7

relationships.condition: Baseline at the deepest/narrowest shape (dmodel/Lb=15), and residual design changes
relationships.reason: Based on Fig. 7 text. At dmodel/Lb=15, baseline loss is 1.926–2.017, about 4–9% above the optimum of 1.847. The optimum also shifts from 60 to 45 with AttnRes, so the best shape depends on residual design.
relationships.display_finding: At width-to-depth ratio 15, baseline loss was 1.926–2.017 versus the optimum 1.847, a 4–9% penalty; AttnRes shifted the optimal ratio from 60 to 45.
